official.description: The Allama Muhammad Iqbal Scholarship Program is a Higher Education Commission of Pakistan initiative aimed at strengthening educational cooperation and cultural ties with Central Asian and friendly nations, offering 350 fully funded scholarships over five years for international students to pursue undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral degree programmes at top-ranked Pakistani universities.

applicant_utility.summary: This is HEC's flagship inbound scheme: 350 fully funded places over five years for nationals of the listed Central Asian and friendly countries, covering tuition in full plus a monthly stipend, an accommodation allowance and airfare as per policy. Eligibility turns on two things - nationality from the published country list, and the academic threshold for undergraduate entry (GCE A Levels or equivalent at 60%, or 65% for Engineering). Because HEC publishes no stipend figure and no standing application window, confirm the current round with the programme office and budget against Pakistani living costs rather than an advertised amount.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Students from the listed Central Asian and friendly countries who want a fully funded undergraduate, postgraduate or doctoral degree at a top-ranked Pakistani university and can obtain an IBCC equivalence certificate.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country appears on HEC's published eligible-country list before investing time in the application
Check your marks against the undergraduate threshold - 60% in GCE A Levels or equivalent, and 65% for Engineering
Plan for the Equivalence Certificate from IBCC Pakistan, which HEC requires once the scholarship is awarded
Pick your field from the published list of disciplines rather than assuming any subject is open
Contact the programme office to confirm whether a round is currently open, since HEC publishes no deadline
Prepare for any test or interview HEC schedules for your level
common_rejection_risks: Nationality outside the published Central Asian and friendly-country list, which is the scheme's defining restriction
Undergraduate marks below 60%, or below 65% for Engineering
Inability to produce an IBCC equivalence certificate, which is a condition of holding the award
Applying when no round is open - with no published standing deadline, a well-prepared file can arrive too early or too late
Assuming the stipend will meet full living costs when HEC publishes no amount
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: HEC publishes no stipend figure, so visa costs, personal expenses and anything above the stipend and accommodation allowance must be self-funded; airfare is covered only 'as per policy'.
document_audit: HEC's programme pages do not list required documents, so obtain the current checklist from the programme office rather than assuming a standard set
The equivalence certificate from IBCC Pakistan is issued after the award, but the underlying A Level or equivalent results must already be verifiable
Because the application is online, scans must be legible and in the formats HEC's portal accepts - confirm the specification before uploading
alerts: No application deadline is published on HEC's programme pages; treat the window as unknown until HEC confirms it
The scheme is multi-year - 350 places over five years - rather than a single annual round, so there is no fixed date to plan around
The airfare and accommodation allowance are granted 'as per policy', so the exact entitlement is set by HEC rules rather than quoted to you in advance

The programme's other components - the undergraduate semester exchange programme, the Pakistan Higher Education Expo in Central Asia, and leadership training for civil servants - are separate from the scholarships for students

applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Confirm that a round is open, apply online through the HEC scholarship portal, pass any required tests or interviews, and obtain the IBCC equivalence certificate after the award.
